_source: AI-researched venue CANDIDATES for Manchester and Cheshire, awaiting review — never directly edited by the research agent. Populated by a daily scheduled research agent (2026-08, at explicit user request: 'fan out some research agents who's goal is to run every day to find and suggest new businesses... they shouldn't go beyond cheshire and manchester just yet'; bumped from ~3-5/day to 10/day at a later explicit request). See .claude/agents/curia-research-daily.md for the full research brief/rules this agent works under (Hard rule 1 chain/fast-food screening, real coordinates only, no duplicates, Do/Drink/Eat coverage balance). The research agent commits straight to master for this file (no PR — this queue has zero effect on the live app, nothing reads it except the review agent and the admin dashboard's Growth Insights context). A second, independent daily agent (.claude/agents/curia-suggestion-review.md) re-verifies each `pending` entry and is the only thing that ever promotes one into the real docs/data/venues.json, behind its own pull request — see that file's own doc comment for why the human checkpoint lives there instead of here. Each entry mirrors docs/data/venues.json's own raw shape (name/district/type/spend/lat/lon/base/bands/reason) exactly, so a reviewed-and-approved entry can be moved into that file with a straight copy-paste, plus review-only fields (suggestedDate, status, researchNotes) that get stripped on promotion. `district` values must be a real existing district id from docs/data/districts.json (manchester/cheshire metros only) UNLESS the entry is itself proposing a brand-new district — see district-suggestions.json for that case instead; a venue suggestion should never invent a district id that doesn't exist anywhere.
_reviewWorkflow: status starts 'pending' on every new entry. The daily curia-suggestion-review agent changes it to 'approved' (then copies the venue fields into docs/data/venues.json and removes the entry here, as part of its own PR) or 'rejected' (left here with researchNotes explaining why, as a record so the same candidate isn't re-suggested later — curia-research-daily checks every entry here regardless of status before suggesting anything new). A human's actual review happens by reading/merging the review agent's PR, not by editing this file directly, though a human reviewer (or a future admin-dashboard screen) can still hand-edit an entry's status here if needed.

suggestions.name: Clark Art
suggestions.reason: Bill Clark's own gallery on Ashley Road since 1999, deep in L.S. Lowry and the northern painters he's written the books on — a private dealer's eye, not a gallery chain's algorithm.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Clark Art (155 Ashley Road, Hale) closed permanently on 3 October 2024 after 18 years, per Bill Clark's own retirement announcement (reported by Altrincham Today, 'An incredible journey: Clark Art to close after 18 years in Hale village'). The prior research pass's sources (Tripadvisor/Artsy/halebarns.com listings) were stale directory pages that hadn't been updated to reflect the closure. Do not re-suggest — the gallery no longer exists.

suggestions.name: Yang Sing
suggestions.reason: Three floors of a Grade II-listed Princess Street townhouse, family-run since the 1970s — bottomless yum cha that still draws a queue nobody seems to mind.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Yang Sing (34 Princess Street) has been closed since December 2021/early 2022 (kitchen fire, then a lease dispute) and Yang Sing Limited is now in liquidation per Companies House — it never reopened despite the owner's 2022 hope to reopen by 2023/24. The prior research pass's sources (visitmanchester.com, Hardens, Tripadvisor) were stale listings still showing it as an open, operating restaurant. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Blue Lobster
suggestions.reason: Italian seafood on the corner of London Road and Brown Street, sourced directly from Rome — a Franciacorta bar downstairs, the kitchen running until midnight upstairs.
suggestions.researchNotes: REJECTED on independent re-verification 2026-09-03: Blue Lobster (34 London Road, Alderley Edge) closed permanently in December 2017, less than nine months after its April 2017 opening, following a staff-payment dispute with owner Andrea Zecchino (reported by alderleyedge.com and Manchester Confidential at the time). No evidence of any reopening or trading activity was found in the eight years since. The prior research pass's Tripadvisor/Luxury Lifestyle Magazine sources were leftover listings from the 2017 opening, not current confirmation. Do not re-suggest unless it demonstrably reopens under new ownership.

suggestions.name: Fire Station Social Cucina
suggestions.reason: A pizza theatre and wood oven where Gusto used to sit on London Road — hand-rolled pasta, Napoli-style bases, and only one other room anywhere doing the same thing.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via thebusinessdesk.com, wilmslow.co.uk/alderleyedge.com and the operator's own site (firestationsocial.co.uk): Fire Station Social Cucina, 75 London Road, Alderley Edge SK9 7DY, opened 10 June 2026 in the former Gusto unit — the second site for this specific concept, after the original in Tarporley. Run by 'Project Social Cucina', the restaurant division of Cheshire Pub Company (a separate entity from the 7-pub Cheshire Cat group already referenced elsewhere in this file) — only 2 sites confirmed under the Fire Station Social Cucina name itself, the same 2-site sibling precedent already used for Cibo/Suburban Green/Smoke Wilmslow/Heddy's/Caramello. Flagged for the reviewer: the parent company's own press describes this as 'expansion', so worth a quick re-check at promotion time that a third site hasn't since appeared. Moderate-high confidence otherwise — real, recently opened, well-covered locally, no closure signals. Re-checked again 2026-09-08 (curia-suggestion-review daily pass) specifically for a rumoured third site: none found — same 2-site status as this note originally recorded, still pending, still in docs/data/pending-review-queue.json for a human call rather than re-decided here. DECIDED 2026-09-08 by direct user instruction, in an interactive session: promoted into venues.json with the new `status: 'coming-soon'` field (added the same day specifically for this case) rather than a flat yes/no — real venue, passes Hard rule 1 on site count today, but its editorial confidence marker stays provisional given the parent's stated expansion plans. See venues.json's own note on the new field.

suggestions.name: Savoy Cinema
suggestions.reason: Art deco since the 1920s, dark for years, reborn in 2015 under the same family who run two more just like it in Belper and Melton Mowbray — 180 velvet seats, a licensed bar, and a programme that still mixes new releases with classics rather than picking one.
suggestions.researchNotes: Heaton Moor had zero venues of any kind before this pass — the most acute district gap found today. Verified via savoycinemaheatonmoor.com (own site), cinematreasures.org and independentcinemaoffice.org.uk: 105 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4HY, run by the Mundin family since 2015, currently trading, own listed events/showtimes. Chain check: the Mundins also run the Ritz Cinema (Belper, Derbyshire) and the Regal Cinema (Melton Mowbray, Leicestershire) — a real 3-site family group across three different towns, no closer geographically than Wallop's existing Knutsford/Prestwich/Didsbury precedent already accepted in this file, so treated the same way rather than as chain territory. Coordinates from the postcode centroid (SK4 4HY), cross-checked via web search against the venue's own street address. High confidence — independently owned, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Heaton Social
suggestions.reason: Shaw Road's old oriental restaurant made over into a wine-and-cocktails room under local ownership since January 2025 — a neat beer garden out back, a function room downstairs, and a landlord whose roots in Heaton Moor go back further than the venue does.
suggestions.researchNotes: Closes Heaton Moor's Drink gap (was zero). Verified via heatonsocial.com (own site), CAMRA's own listing and whatpub.com: 3 Shaw Road, Heaton Moor SK4 4AG. Reopened 14 January 2025 as Heaton Social under new independent local ownership ('Jack'), previously traded as 'Pale' from 2018 — a change of hands, not a rebrand of a chain. No sibling sites found anywhere. Coordinates from the SK4 4AG postcode centroid. High confidence — currently trading, well-documented, single-site.

suggestions.name: Cure Bistro
suggestions.reason: Mehmed and David's own room on Heaton Moor Road since May last year — a rotating French and Mediterranean menu with the cocktail list treated as seriously as the kitchen, not bolted on as an afterthought.
suggestions.researchNotes: Closes Heaton Moor's Eat gap (was zero). Verified via curebistro.co.uk (own site), stockport.nub.news's opening feature and the Food Standards Agency ratings register (business live and rated): 110 Heaton Moor Road, Stockport SK4 4NZ, opened 2 May 2025, co-owned by Mehmed and David. No sibling sites found. Introduces a new type, 'FRENCH BISTRO' — no existing type/tile fits a French-and-Mediterranean bistro-bar precisely (GASTROPUB is the closest existing Eat type but implies a British pub kitchen, which this isn't); left category-only (Eat), same treatment as CANTONESE ROAST/GREEK TAVERNA elsewhere in this file. Coordinates from the SK4 4NZ postcode centroid. High confidence — recently opened, well-documented, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Bar Caput
suggestions.reason: The same two chefs who earned Cantaloupe its Michelin Bib Gourmand have reopened the same Great Underbank room as a Roman aperitivo bar — fritti, osteria plates and a cocktail called the Bicycle Thief, built to be a Tuesday habit rather than a once-a-year booking.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via themanc.com, thecaterer.com, restaurantonline.co.uk and hardens.com: Cantaloupe (71 Great Underbank, Stockport SK1 1PE), a genuine Michelin Bib Gourmand restaurant, served its final dinner 8 August 2026 and reopened at the same address as Bar Caput on 26 August 2026 — same owner-chefs (Joshua Reed-Cooper and Mike Thomas), new Roman-inspired concept. Treated as a real, distinct new business per this file's own Sugo/Sud precedent (a genuinely different concept needs its own verification, not inherited trust) — but here the operators are unchanged and independently confirmed single-site, so this is a same-owner relaunch rather than an unrelated successor tenant. No other Bar Caput locations found. Coordinates from the SK1 1PE postcode centroid (same building as the former Cantaloupe). High confidence — very recently opened (2 weeks old at research time), heavily covered by trade and local press, no closure signals since opening.

suggestions.name: Trattoria D'Agostino
suggestions.reason: Marco D'Agostino's own kitchen on Station Road since 2010, family-run and single-site by choice — a quarter-century of Italian cooking behind a menu that never bothered opening a second dining room to prove it.
suggestions.researchNotes: Cheadle Hulme's Eat category was its thinnest (1 venue, Delhi Dream) before this pass. Verified via trattoria-d.co.uk (own site), opentable.co.uk (hours confirmed set 20/06/2026) and Companies House (Trattoria D'Agostino Limited, active): 16a Station Road, Cheadle Hulme SK8 5AE, founded 2010 by chef Marco D'Agostino, over 25 years' culinary experience. No sibling sites found anywhere — genuinely single-site, unlike the several Cheadle Hulme pub candidates already rejected in this file for tied-house/chain ownership (Ye Olde Admiral Rodney, Church Inn, Village Pub & Grill, John Millington). Coordinates from the SK8 5AE postcode centroid. High confidence — recent review activity (Nov 2025) confirms still trading, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Sip Wine Bar
suggestions.reason: Nick Yates' Enomatic wall on Burton Road, pouring by the glass so you can try before committing to the bottle — cheese and charcuterie built to match, and regulars who've learned by now to book.
suggestions.researchNotes: Didsbury's Drink category was its thinnest (1 venue, Saison) before this pass. Verified via sipwine.co.uk (own site), tripadvisor.co.uk (2026 reviews, current hours confirmed) and tasteofmanchester.com: 156 Burton Road, West Didsbury, Manchester M20 1LH, owned and run by Nick Yates (25+ years in the wine/restaurant trade). Confirmed independent, single-site, no sibling locations found — distinct from the already-noted West Didsbury original of Wilmslow's Suburban Green (a different business). Also confirmed The Violet Hour, which some listings still show at a nearby Burton Road address, was in fact rebranded to Saison (already seeded in this file) years ago and no longer exists under that name — checked specifically to avoid suggesting a stale/closed venue. Coordinates from the M20 1LH postcode centroid. High confidence — active listings, recent reviews, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: Prestbury Golf Club
suggestions.reason: A Harry Colt course laid out on Macclesfield Road in 1920, good enough to sit inside England's top hundred — a proper members' round a mile past the Village's antique shops and timbered pubs.
suggestions.researchNotes: Prestbury's Do category was its thinnest (1 venue, Rococo, a shop rather than an activity) before this pass. Verified via prestburygolfclub.com (own site), top100golfcourses.com and leadingcourses.com: Macclesfield Road, Prestbury SK10 4BJ, founded 1920, Harry Colt-designed course, independent members' club (not part of any group). Same real-institution precedent already established for Wilmslow Golf Club (GOLF CLUB type) elsewhere in this file. Coordinates from the SK10 4BJ postcode centroid. High confidence — well-documented, actively operating private club, no closure signals (golf clubs of this standing don't carry closure risk the way hospitality venues do).

suggestions.name: The Beer House
suggestions.reason: Manchester Road's cask specialist since 2000, sold out of the Marble Brewery stable in 2018 and free of any tie since — four years running as Trafford & Hulme CAMRA's own Pub of the Year, and a patio that fills before the taps do.
suggestions.researchNotes: Verified via camra.org.uk, morningadvertiser.co.uk ('Marble sells its Beerhouse', 2018) and the venue's own thebeerhousechorlton.co.uk: 57 Manchester Road, Chorlton-cum-Hardy M21 9PW. Opened 2000 as The Marble Beer House; Marble Brewery sold it in 2018 to new owner Alex Price, who runs it independently — Marble beers still feature as one of several guest lines, not as tied ownership. Confirmed single-site, no other locations. Coordinates from the M21 9PW postcode centroid. High confidence — active CAMRA listing, ongoing Pub of the Year recognition, no closure signals. (Separately checked and ruled out for Chorlton: Fell Bar Chorlton, part of a 5-site Fell Brewery taproom group spanning Kendal/Penrith/Chorlton/Northern Quarter/Stockport — too wide a footprint to pass Hard rule 1.)

suggestions.name: The Garden Eatery
suggestions.reason: Kate's own plant-led room on Ashley Road since 2014 — daytime only, dairy and meat optional rather than absent, and a queue for the sweetcorn fritters that starts most mornings before ten.
suggestions.researchNotes: Hale's Eat category was its joint-thinnest (2 venues, Victors and Charlie Brown's Hale) before this pass. Verified via thegardeneatery.co.uk / thegardeneateryhale.co.uk (own sites), manchestersfinest.com and opentable.co.uk: 154 Ashley Road, Hale WA15 9SA, opened 9 December 2014, founded by Kate and a co-founder, plant-led daytime menu with meat/fish/dairy add-ins. No sibling sites found — genuinely single-site, distinct from Piccolino and COOK (both ruled out on the same street/area search for being national chains). Coordinates from the WA15 9SA postcode centroid. High confidence — long-established (11 years trading), active current listings, no closure signals.

suggestions.name: The Edge
suggestions.reason: The wooded sandstone ridge the whole village takes its name from, National Trust-managed since 1948 — Engine Vein and the Druids' Circle a fifteen-minute walk apart, real caves nobody's quite meant to still be exploring, and the actual reason The Wizard's regulars turn up muddy.
suggestions.researchNotes: Alderley Edge's Do category was its thinnest (2 venues, Manchester Rare Books and Festival Hall) before this pass. Verified via nationaltrust.org.uk (own listing, 'Alderley Edge and Cheshire Countryside'): a National Trust-owned and -managed woodland ridge on Macclesfield Road, open year-round, near postcode SK10 4UB. Not a commercial chain — a charitable heritage body, same category of inclusion already accepted for council-owned parks (The Carrs, Fletcher Moss, Marie Louise Gardens, Chorlton Water Park, Bruntwood Park, Thorn Grove Park) elsewhere in this file; this is the specific real landmark the district and several of its existing venues (The Wizard, The Old Cellars) already reference by name in their own copy, not a new invented attraction. Introduces a new type, 'NATURE RESERVE' — no existing type fits a wooded heritage ridge (RIVERSIDE PARK implies a riverside, which this isn't); left category-only (Do), same treatment as TOWN PARK/FARM EXPERIENCE elsewhere in this file. Named 'The Edge' rather than 'Alderley Edge' to avoid colliding with the district's own name, matching the district's own editorial description's phrasing ('the actual Edge — the wooded ridge, not a marketing name'). Coordinates from the SK10 4UB postcode centroid (the National Trust car park end, Nether Alderley side). High confidence — a National Trust property, no closure risk in the ordinary commercial sense.
